title: AI-Assisted Refactoring & Code Modernization
description: Master AI-driven code refactoring in .NET 9 and C# 13: migrating legacy synchronous patterns to async/await, adopting modern language features, eliminating anti-patterns, and validating equivalence with characterization testing.

data.text: The Engineering Discipline of AI-Driven Refactoring

Refactoring enterprise .NET codebases using Large Language Models is fundamentally different from greenfield generation. When modernizing legacy C# code (e.g., migrating .NET Framework 4.8 monoliths to .NET 9, converting synchronous blocking calls to non-blocking async/await, or replacing complex class hierarchies with records and pattern matching), the primary risk is silent semantic drift: subtle behavioral alterations, broken exception contracts, or altered synchronization contexts that pass compilation but fail in production under concurrent load.

data.caption: The Five-Stage AI Refactoring Verification Loop
data.code:
graph TD
    A[Legacy .NET Code] --> B[Generate Characterization / Approval Tests]
    B --> C[Run Baseline Suite: Green 100%]
    C --> D[Targeted Prompting with Architectural Guardrails]
    D --> E[LLM Refactoring: Modern C# 13 / .NET 9]
    E --> F[Automated Static Analysis & Roslyn Analyzers]
    F -->|Diagnostics Fail| D
    F -->|Diagnostics Clean| G[Run Characterization Suite]
    G -->|Regression Detected| D
    G -->|All Green| H[BenchmarkDotNet Memory / Latency Check]
    H --> I[PR with Automated Diff Review]

data.text: Before asking Copilot or an LLM to refactor a single line of business logic, you must capture the existing code's actual runtime behavior—including edge cases and quirky error handling. Michael Feathers defined characterization tests as tests that capture the current behavior of the system, whether intended or not. In modern .NET, snapshot testing libraries such as Verify.Xunit or Snapper provide ideal mechanisms to lock in outputs before modernization.

data.title: Legacy C# Service to Modernize
data.content: Consider this legacy financial calculation service written in C# 7 / .NET Framework style with synchronous blocking, mutable state, and archaic serialization.

data.text: When prompting AI for refactoring, vague prompts like 'make this modern C#' result in unpredictable mutations. Production refactoring requires explicit prompt constraints enforcing targeted language constructs (e.g., C# 13 collection expressions, pattern matching with switch expressions, immutable records, primary constructors, and zero-allocation span operations).

data.title: Refactoring Prompt Template & .NET 9 Result
data.content: The system prompt must enforce semantic equivalence, pure functional refactoring, and Roslyn safety analyzers.

data.title: Injecting TimeProvider for Testability
data.content: Notice how the AI modernized the static `DateTime.UtcNow` into .NET 8/9's `TimeProvider`. This eliminates non-deterministic tests and enables precise unit test mocking without brittle third-party wrapper shims.

data.text: To guarantee that the refactored code produces identical outputs across all possible transaction permutations, use snapshot testing before and after refactoring.

data.title: Equivalence Snapshot Test in xUnit
data.content: Snapshot tests serialize the output to disk and diff it on every test execution. If the AI introduced even a microsecond or fractional penny change, the test fails instantly.

data.caption: AI Refactoring Traps and Engineering Countermeasures
rows: Unobserved task exceptions crash the IIS/K8s host process
Explicit rule: 'Never introduce async void; return Task or ValueTask exclusively.'
LINQ deferred execution causes repeated database queries or mutated state
Rule: 'Use ReadOnlySpan<T>, IReadOnlyList<T>, or materialise with .ToList() before iteration.'
AI replaces domain-specific exceptions with generic InvalidOperationException
Rule: 'Preserve exact custom exception hierarchies and inner exception chaining.'
Changing property names, casing, or visibility breaks external API JSON contracts
Rule: 'Maintain JSON serialization attributes (JsonPropertyName) and field casing.'
Removing Null Checks Without Nullable Context
Removing guards causes NullReferenceException when NRT is disabled upstream
Rule: 'Verify nullable annotations match csproj <Nullable>enable</Nullable> settings.'

data.text: Refactoring should improve maintainability without compromising throughput or memory allocation. Use BenchmarkDotNet to measure the before-and-after performance of AI-refactored methods.

data.title: BenchmarkDotNet Verification Harness
data.content: Verify that moving to `ReadOnlySpan<T>` and ref readonly struct eliminated GC heap allocations on the critical processing path.

data.title: Production AI Refactoring Checklist
items: Capture characterization tests (approval snapshots) before prompting any changes
Specify target language version (C# 13 / .NET 9) and framework conventions in prompt
Enforce zero changes to public API signatures and JSON serialization contracts
Ensure Roslyn analyzers (CA rules, stylecop, nullable warnings) run clean with zero warnings
Validate async/await transformations: no async void, proper CancellationToken propagation
Run BenchmarkDotNet to ensure memory allocations did not regress
Review git diff line-by-line; do not accept wholesale rewritten files without scrutiny

data.title: Summary & Next Steps
points: AI refactoring is most powerful when guided by strict architectural and syntactic boundaries.
Characterization tests (Verify.Xunit) eliminate the risk of silent behavioral regressions.
Modernizing legacy code to C# 13 with primary constructors, pattern matching, and spans reduces heap churn.
Always benchmark critical paths to guarantee performance improvements alongside clean code.
data.takeaway: Treat AI as an accelerator for syntax modernization, but rely on characterization tests and Roslyn analyzers as the immutable guardians of semantic correctness.
